block_row: [EXISTS] VC707 SoC top. A VexRiscv CPU runs firmware from an instruction memory and reaches a data memory and the accelerator register window through an address decoder; the accelerator window is converted to AXI4-Lite by a bridge. The MHSA accelerator is the only block that reads DRAM (MIG DDR3, external) for tensor data; the CPU never touches tensor data.

frame_row: [EXISTS] VC707 SoC top. A VexRiscv CPU runs firmware from an instruction memory and reaches a data memory and the accelerator register window through an address decoder; the accelerator window is converted to AXI4-Lite by a bridge. The MHSA accelerator is the only block that reads DRAM (MIG DDR3, external) for tensor data; the CPU never touches tensor data.

label: u_cpu
(VexRiscv)
blocks.function: [EXISTS] RV32 CPU. It fetches instructions on its instruction bus and issues one data-bus transaction at a time. In this system its firmware only writes the task configuration into the accelerator registers, sets START and polls the DONE flag; it never moves tensor data.

label: u_dec
(dbus_decoder)
blocks.function: [EXISTS] Address decoder of the data bus. Accesses to the low 64 KiB go to the data memory; accesses to the 0x4xxx_xxxx window go to the bridge. It returns the response of the selected target to the CPU.

label: u_bridge
(Bridge)
blocks.function: [EXISTS] Converts a single data-bus command into one AXI4-Lite read or write transaction and returns the read data or write response. Verified at 5 cycles per write and 4 per read.

label: u_acc
(mhsa_accelerator)
blocks.function: [FIXED] Multi-head self-attention engine (D = 768, 12 heads of 64, INT8, assumed). After START its own controller requests contiguous chunks (X, then Wq, Wk, Wv in three 768 x 256 chunks each) from DRAM through a read-only DMA, runs the tile GEMM core and the softmax unit, and reports DONE or ERR in its status register. v0 is sequential: load, then compute. Expanded on page 02.

label: u_imem
(IMEM)
blocks.function: [EXISTS] 64 KiB instruction memory at 0x8000_0000, wired to the instruction bus only (Harvard), so the firmware has no initialised data section.

label: u_dmem
(DMEM)
blocks.function: [EXISTS] 64 KiB data memory at 0x0000_0000 for stack and control variables; it never holds tensor data.

interfaces.name: Instruction bus
interfaces.signals: cmd_valid, cmd_ready, cmd_pc[31:0]; u_imem -> u_cpu: rsp_valid, rsp_inst[31:0]

interfaces.name: Data bus
interfaces.signals: cmd_valid, cmd_ready, cmd_wr, cmd_address[31:0], cmd_data[31:0], cmd_mask[3:0], cmd_size[1:0]; u_dec -> u_cpu: rsp_ready, rsp_data[31:0]

interfaces.name: DMEM port
interfaces.signals: sel, we, addr, wdata[31:0], mask[3:0]; u_dmem -> u_dec: rdata[31:0]

interfaces.name: Bridge command
interfaces.signals: cmd_valid, cmd_ready, cmd_wr, cmd_addr[31:0], cmd_data[31:0], cmd_mask[3:0]; u_bridge -> u_dec: rsp_valid, rsp_data[31:0]

interfaces.name: AXI4-Lite
interfaces.signals: AWADDR, AWPROT, AWVALID, AWREADY, WDATA, WSTRB, WVALID, WREADY, BRESP, BVALID, BREADY, ARADDR, ARPROT, ARVALID, ARREADY, RDATA, RRESP, RVALID, RREADY

interfaces.name: AXI4 read
interfaces.signals: ARADDR, ARLEN, ARSIZE, ARBURST, ARID, ARVALID, ARREADY; DRAM -> u_acc: RDATA (32 bit debug, 512 bit target), RRESP, RLAST, RID, RVALID, RREADY

interfaces.name: Clock and reset
interfaces.signals: clk, rst (one clock domain assumed in v0)
